vuln_id: ARVO arvo:1461 / libxml2 xmlAddDefAttrs non-flexible tail array

classification.classification_note: The vulnerable code logically allocates room for multiple default-attribute tuples, but `_xmlDefAttrs.values` is declared as the fixed member `const xmlChar *values[5]`. When the same element receives a second defaulted attribute, `xmlAddDefAttrs()` computes base index 5 on that declared five-element member and UBSan reports the out-of-bounds write.

bug_description.original: The use of non-flexible array members in parser.c triggers spurious UBSan errors, potentially leading to incorrect handling of memory or undefined behavior during parsing operations.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 37-byte witness `<!DOCTYPE[<!ATTLISTN S ID\t'' :\tID\t'' ` reaches `xmlParseAttributeListDecl` through the saved stack `xmlDoRead -> xmlParseDocument -> xmlParseInternalSubset -> xmlParseMarkupDecl -> xmlParseAttributeListDecl`. Inside that parser, line 6093 first materializes `elemName = N`; the first loop iteration then parses attribute `S` with explicit default `''`, so line 6181 calls `xmlAddDefAttrs()` and creates an `xmlDefAttrs` record keyed by element `N`. That record is logically sized for four default attributes (`maxAttrs = 4`), but its type still declares `const xmlChar *values[5]`. The same malformed `ATTLIST` bytes then yield a second attribute `:` with another explicit default `''`; the second `xmlAddDefAttrs()` call reuses the same record, the only present guard `defaults->nbAttrs >= defaults->maxAttrs` remains false (`1 >= 4`), and the store `defaults->values[5 * defaults->nbAttrs] = name;` uses subscript 5 on the declared five-element member. Stage 01 reproduces `UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: runtime error: index 5 out of bounds for type 'const xmlChar *[5]'` at `parser.c:1282:5`. The staged patch changes `_xmlDefAttrs.values` to a flexible array member so the declared extent matches the variable-length tail allocation.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the staged witness into vulnerability-relevant parser state by materializing the element name later reused as the hash key for both default-attribute insertions.
source.value_from: In the exact 37-byte PoC `<!DOCTYPE[<!ATTLISTN S ID\t'' :\tID\t'' `, the byte after `<!ATTLIST` is `N`. Even though lines 6088-6091 report the missing required space, the function continues and line 6093 still consumes that byte as `elemName = "N"`.
source.note: This is the scored source rather than the later `xmlAddDefAttrs()` call because it is the first project statement that creates the parser state (`elemName`) reused across both insertions into `ctxt->attsDefault`.

root_cause.description: The root cause is the fixed member declaration `values[5]` in `_xmlDefAttrs`. `xmlAddDefAttrs()` later treats the member as a variable-length tail array indexed in 5-pointer groups per logical attribute, so the second logical attribute already starts one element past the declared bound.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this exact declaration to `const xmlChar *values[];` under C99, aligning the declared extent with the variable-length allocation strategy.

sink.description: UBSan crash site. On the second insertion into the same `xmlDefAttrs` record, this store computes subscript 5 on the declared `values[5]` member.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace and `reproduction_report.json` both identify `parser.c:1282:5` in `xmlAddDefAttrs` with summary `index 5 out of bounds for type 'const xmlChar *[5]'`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Each `''` token in the staged PoC is materialized here as a non-NULL empty-string `defaultValue`. Those explicit defaults, together with `elemName` and the parsed attribute names, are what satisfy the `xmlAddDefAttrs()` gate twice inside the same `<!ATTLIST N ...>` loop.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The exact witness contains two such tokens: one after `S ID` and one after `:\tID`.
tainted_value_origin.note: Stage 02 evidence is limited to these two empty-string defaults from the staged 37-byte witness.

parser_admitted.description: After the witness opens a malformed internal subset with `<!DOCTYPE[`, the next markup declaration begins with `<!ATTLIST`, so `xmlParseMarkupDecl()` dispatches into `xmlParseAttributeListDecl()`, the parser that reaches the saved UBSan crash.

coarse_trace.summary: The 37-byte witness opens an internal subset and presents `<!ATTLIST...`, so libxml2 dispatches into `xmlParseAttributeListDecl()` despite the malformed DTD syntax.
The attribute-list parser materializes `elemName = N`, then parses the first defaulted attribute `S ''` and calls `xmlAddDefAttrs()` because the declaration carries an explicit default value.
The first call allocates an `xmlDefAttrs` record for element `N`, stores the first 5-pointer tuple, and leaves `nbAttrs = 1`.
The same `ATTLIST` body still contains `:\tID\t''`, so the loop parses a second explicit defaulted attribute for the same element and makes a second `xmlAddDefAttrs()` call.

The second call reuses the same record; the only guard `defaults->nbAttrs >= defaults->maxAttrs` stays false, but the reused object still exposes `values[5]`, so the base store at line 1282 hits out-of-bounds index 5 and matches the saved UBSan report.

fine_trace.note: Source. After `<!ATTLIST`, the staged witness materializes `elemName = "N"`. That value is later passed unchanged into both `xmlAddDefAttrs()` calls and becomes the hash key that makes the second call reuse the first call's `xmlDefAttrs` record.
On the first loop iteration, the bytes `S ID\t''` produce `attrName = "S"`, materializing the first attribute name before any call to `xmlAddDefAttrs()`.

Still on that first `AttDef`, `xmlParseDefaultDecl` consumes the first `''` token and returns a non-NULL empty-string `defaultValue`; `def` is an explicit default, so the later `xmlAddDefAttrs()` gate is eligible.
Because `ctxt->sax2` is active, `defaultValue != NULL`, and `def` is neither `#IMPLIED` nor `#REQUIRED`, the first parsed tuple `N / S / ""` is handed to `xmlAddDefAttrs()` for persistent storage.

fine_trace.var: fullname, name, prefix, defaults, defaults->nbAttrs, defaults->maxAttrs
fine_trace.note: The first call resolves `fullname = elemName = "N"` to hash key `name = "N", prefix = NULL`, finds no existing defaults record, allocates one object with logical room for four 5-pointer tuples, initializes `nbAttrs = 0` and `maxAttrs = 4`, and inserts it into `ctxt->attsDefault` under that element key.

fine_trace.var: fullattr, name, prefix, defaults->values, defaults->nbAttrs, value
fine_trace.note: Inside that first `xmlAddDefAttrs()` call, `fullattr = "S"` resolves to `name = "S", prefix = NULL`; with `defaults->nbAttrs == 0`, the stores fill indices 0 through 4 of the tuple and then increment `nbAttrs` to 1.
The same `ATTLIST` body still has remaining bytes `:\tID\t'' ` before any closing `>`, so a second loop iteration materializes `attrName = ":"` for the same element `N`.
On that second `AttDef`, the next `''` token again yields a non-NULL empty-string `defaultValue`, so the second attribute also qualifies as an explicit default.
The parser therefore makes a second `xmlAddDefAttrs()` call with the original `elemName = "N"` and the second attribute tuple `: / ""`.

The second call resolves the same element key `N`, reuses the previously allocated `defaults` record, and checks only `defaults->nbAttrs >= defaults->maxAttrs`. After step 6, `nbAttrs == 1` and `maxAttrs == 4`, so that guard is false and no reallocation or bounds correction occurs.

Root cause. The live record reused in step 10 still inherits `_xmlDefAttrs.values[5]` as its declared destination extent. The over-allocation from step 5 only provides extra tail bytes; it does not change this member's five-element C type, so index 5 is already out of bounds.

Sink. On the second insertion, lines 1273-1279 resolve `fullattr = ":"` to `name = ":"`; `defaults->nbAttrs` is still 1, so the base subscript becomes `5 * 1 = 5`. Because step 11 fixes the destination extent to `values[5]`, this write lands one element past the declared member and matches the saved UBSan report `index 5 out of bounds for type 'const xmlChar *[5]'` at `parser.c:1282:5`.

poc.trigger: Feeding the staged 37-byte `poc` to the vulnerable `libxml2_xml_read_memory_fuzzer` makes libxml2 parse one malformed `<!ATTLIST` for element `N` with two explicit defaulted attributes, so `xmlAddDefAttrs()` runs twice on the same `xmlDefAttrs` record and reproduces the saved `UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: index 5 out of bounds for type 'const xmlChar *[5]'` report at `parser.c:1282:5`.
